title: Yellowing of Eyes
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with painless jaundice, dark urine, clay-colored stools, pruritus, and weight loss — classic for malignant biliary obstruction. Courvoisier's sign: palpable, non-tender gallbladder in a jaundiced patient = malignancy until proven otherwise (most commonly pancreatic head adenocarcinoma). Pancreatic cancer most commonly arises in the head of the pancreas (70%), causing early obstructive jaundice. Late presentation is the rule — most are unresectable at diagnosis. Workup: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast (pancreatic protocol — dual-phase) for staging. CA 19-9 tumor marker (not diagnostic but prognostic and monitors recurrence). ERCP/MRCP for biliary drainage if needed. Biopsy via EUS-FNA. If resectable (localized, no vascular involvement, no mets): pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure). If unresectable: palliative biliary stenting, chemotherapy (gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel or FOLFIRINOX). Poor prognosis — 5-year survival <10%.
chief_complaint: Painless jaundice, weight loss, dark urine, clay-colored stools

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Abdomen
stacks.finding: Courvoisier's sign: palpable non-tender gallbladder in jaundiced patient. RUQ mass.

stacks.label: BMP / CMP / LFTs
stacks.finding: Obstructive pattern: elevated ALP, GGT, direct bilirubin. AST/ALT mildly elevated.

stacks.label: CA 19-9
stacks.finding: Tumor marker. Prognostic + monitors treatment response. Not diagnostic (false positives in cholangitis, pancreatitis).

stacks.label: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast (pancreatic protocol)
stacks.finding: Dual-phase CT for pancreatic mass, vascular involvement, liver mets. Most important staging study.

stacks.label: EUS with FNA
stacks.finding: Tissue diagnosis. Endoscopic ultrasound with fine needle aspiration of pancreatic mass.

stacks.label: ERCP / MRCP
stacks.finding: Imaging of biliary tree. Therapeutic: biliary stent if obstruction.

stacks.label: Consult, oncology / Surgical oncology
stacks.finding: Multidisciplinary decision: resectable (Whipple) vs palliative chemotherapy.

stacks.label: Refer to palliative care
stacks.finding: Pancreatic cancer has poor prognosis — early palliative care improves QOL.

physical_exam.abdominal: Courvoisier's sign: palpable, non-tender gallbladder. Epigastric mass possible. Hepatomegaly from biliary obstruction.

decoys.label: MRI as first-line for pancreatic mass
decoys.reason_wrong: CT with pancreatic protocol (dual-phase, IV contrast) is first-line. MRI is second-line when CT is equivocal or patient cannot receive contrast.

teach_me_steps.order: Courvoisier's sign = malignancy until proven otherwise
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Painless jaundice + palpable non-tender gallbladder = pancreatic head adenocarcinoma. Gallstones cause pain, so painless distended gallbladder is malignant obstruction.
CT for staging (vascular involvement, mets). EUS-FNA for tissue diagnosis. CA 19-9 for monitoring.

case_summary: Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma. Painless jaundice + Courvoisier's sign. CT pancreatic protocol + EUS-FNA → Whipple if resectable, palliative chemo/stent if not. Poor prognosis. Early palliative care.
